headline: Penobscot County card spending draws scrutiny amid budget crisis
dek: A Bangor Daily News review found more than 1,700 county credit-card purchases totaling over $350,000 in 2025 as officials confronted a multimillion-dollar shortfall.
body: Penobscot County officials charged more than $350,000 to county-issued credit cards in 2025, according to a Bangor Daily News review of records obtained through Maine’s Freedom of Access Act. The review found more than 1,700 purchases, including charges for items ranging from spices to computer software.

The spending took place while the county was confronting a multimillion-dollar shortfall. Department heads, county commissioners and the county administrator used the cards, the Bangor Daily News reported. Most of the purchases were paid with property-tax revenue, while some were reimbursed through Department of Homeland Security grants or other outside funding.

The records do not establish that every purchase was improper. But the newspaper’s review described a permissive spending culture and a lack of policies that could have helped county leaders limit unnecessary costs. The card spending was a small share of the county’s roughly $35 million budget, while still providing a detailed view of spending controls during a fiscal crisis.

Penobscot County’s posted 2026 budget totals $35.4 million. The budget includes a $12.6 million Jail CAP line and shows that line rising 46.77% from the 2025 budget. Earlier reporting by the Bangor Daily News identified jail costs as a central driver of the county’s broader financial problems.

The newly disclosed records give residents a closer look at how county money was used before the 2026 budget took effect. They also add detail to an ongoing debate over whether county officials have adequate rules and oversight for public spending while they work through the budget shortfall.
author: NorthEast News Desk
